'''Sir Steven Charles Cowley''' (born 1959) is a British [[nuclear fusion|fusion]] and astrophysical theoretical [[plasma physics|plasma physicist]]. He has served as director of the [[UKAEA]] [[Culham Centre for Fusion Energy]] between 2009 and 2016,<ref name="ukgbio"/> and as director of the [[United States Department of Energy]] (DOE) [[Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory]] (PPPL) since 1 July 2018.<ref>{{cite web |title=Steven Cowley named director of DOE's Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory |url=https://www.pppl.gov/news/2018/05/steven-cowley-named-director-doe%E2%80%99s-princeton-plasma-physics-laboratory |website=Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory |access-date=16 June 2018 |date=16 May 2018 |archive-date=28 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210928132112/https://www.pppl.gov/news/2018/05/steven-cowley-named-director-doe%E2%80%99s-princeton-plasma-physics-laboratory }}</ref>

Cowley is also a member of the Commission on the Scaling of Fusion Energy,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Meet the Commissioners |url=https://fusion.scsp.ai/commissioners |access-date=29 September 2025 |website=The Commission on the Scaling of Fusion Energy}}</ref> a 12-month effort to create a shared vision for government, academia, and industry on fusion.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About |url=https://fusion.scsp.ai/about |access-date=29 September 2025 |website=The Commission on the Scaling of Fusion Energy}}</ref> In May 2024, he was appointed the chair of the board of trustees for the Faraday Institution.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sir Steven Cowley |url=https://www.faraday.ac.uk/board-trustees/steven-cowley/ |access-date=19 September 2025 |publisher=The Faraday Institute}}</ref> Previously he served as president of [[Corpus Christi College, Oxford]], since October 2016.<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who | title=Cowley, Prof. Steven | doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U261946|id = U261946 | year = 2016 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref>

Cowley's research interests are in [[Plasma (physics)|plasmas]] and [[nuclear fusion]], in [[astrophysical plasma]]s and the laboratory, such as the [[Joint European Torus]] (JET) and the [[ITER|International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER)]].<ref name="googlescholar"/><ref>{{Scopus id }}</ref><ref name="HamConnor2013">{{cite journal|last1=Ham|first1=C J|last2=Connor|first2=J W|last3=Cowley|first3=S C|last4=Hastie|first4=R J|last5=Hender|first5=T C|last6=Liu|first6=Y Q|title=The role of pressure flattening in calculating tearing mode stability|journal=Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion|volume=55|issue=12|year=2013|article-number=125015|issn=0741-3335|doi=10.1088/0741-3335/55/12/125015|arxiv=1308.2070|bibcode=2013PPCF...55l5015H|s2cid=119516411 }}</ref><ref name="SchekochihinCowley2009">{{cite journal|last1=Schekochihin|first1=A. ==Education==
Cowley won a scholarship to [[Corpus Christi College, Oxford]] and graduated with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in physics in 1981.<ref name=whoswho/> He went on to study at [[Princeton University]] as a [[Harkness Fellowship|Harkness Fellow]] and was awarded a PhD in 1985 for research into [[tokamak]]s supervised by [[:en:Russell Kulsrud|Russell Kulsrud]].<ref name="mathgene"/><ref name="phd">{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Steven Charles|last=Cowley |title=Some Aspects of Anomalous Transport in Tokamaks: Stochastic Magnetic Fields, Tearing Modes and Nonlinear Ballooning Instabilities (Convection) |publisher=Princeton University |year=1985 |author-link=Steven Cowley|oclc=77633911|id={{ProQuest|303381032}}}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ccfe.ac.uk/researcher_detail.aspx?id=27|title=Professor Steve Cowley|publisher=Culham Centre for Fusion Energy|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150416090354/http://www.ccfe.ac.uk/researcher_detail.aspx?id=27|archive-date=2015-04-16}}</ref><ref name=ted2>{{TED speaker|steven_cowley}}</ref>

==Career and research==

=== Early Career ===

Following his PhD, Cowley completed [[postdoctoral research]] at the [[Culham Centre for Fusion Energy]] (CCFE). He returned to Princeton in 1987 and joined the faculty at [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA) in 1993, becoming [[full professor]] in 2000. At [[Imperial College, London]], Cowley led the [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]] group from 2001 to 2003, while also serving as a part-time professor.<ref name=govuk>{{cite web|url=https://www.gov.uk/government/people/steven-cowley|title=Chief Executive Officer, Professor Steven Cowley|publisher=gov.uk|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304000344/https://www.gov.uk/government/people/steven-cowley|archive-date=2016-03-04}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Davies |first=Sean |date=16 May 2011 |title=Q and A – Steve Cowley – Culham Centre for Fusion Energy |url=http://eandt.theiet.org/magazine/2011/05/steve-cowley.cfm |journal=E&T: Engineering and Technology Magazine |publisher=The Institution of Engineering and Technology |volume=6 |issue=5 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714122655/http://eandt.theiet.org/magazine/2011/05/steve-cowley.cfm |archive-date=14 July 2014 }}</ref>

===UKAEA CEO===

He was appointed as the head of the EURATOM / CCFE Fusion Association in September 2008 and as CEO of UKAEA in November 2009. In this role, he was head of the UK's national fusion laboratory, the [[Culham Centre for Fusion Energy]] (CCFE). In this time, he oversaw the operation of the world-leading JET tokamak, a joint venture with other European countries (EURATOM). He also oversaw the operation of the UK's national flagship fusion experiment, the [[Mega Ampere Spherical Tokamak|MAST]] tokamak, which entered service in December 1999. His term as director saw the full experimental lifetime of MAST, which ceased operation in 2013, and part of the construction period of its successor, [[MAST Upgrade]].

On 21 July 2015, Cowley gave evidence to a one-off evidence session of the UK House of Lords Science and Technology Select Committee, alongside Dr. David Kingham of the [[Tokamak Energy]] startup, one topic being the adequacy of government support for private fusion ventures.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://committees.parliament.uk/committee/193/science-and-technology-committee/news/93417/nuclear-fusion-research/|title=Academics questioned on nuclear fusion research|date=17 July 2015|publisher=UK Parliament}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://committees.parliament.uk/oralevidence/4674/pdf/|title=Revised transcript of evidence taken before The Select Committee on Science and Technology Inquiry on Nuclear Fusion|date=21 July 2015|publisher=House of Lords, UK Parliament}}</ref> Cowley left CCFE in 2016.<ref name="ukgbio">{{cite web|url=https://www.gov.uk/government/people/steven-cowley|title=Biography, Professor Steven Cowley FRS FREng|publisher=UK Government}}</ref>

=== Oxford University ===

On 18 March 2015, he was elected the [[List of presidents of Corpus Christi College, Oxford|31st President]] of [[Corpus Christi College, Oxford]], his alma mater: he took up the post on 1 October 2016. He is the first scientist to hold the post.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ccc.ox.ac.uk/News/a/Corpus-announces-the-election-of-its-next-President/|title=Corpus announces the election of its next President|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150421191159/http://www.ccc.ox.ac.uk/News/a/Corpus-announces-the-election-of-its-next-President/|archive-date=2015-04-21|publisher=Corpus Christi College|location=Oxford}}</ref>

===PPPL director===

On 1 July 2018, he was appointed director of the [[Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory]] (PPPL).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.princeton.edu/news/2018/05/16/steven-cowley-named-director-does-princeton-plasma-physics-laboratory|date=2018-05-16|title=Steven Cowley named director of DOE's Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180516154600/https://www.princeton.edu/news/2018/05/16/steven-cowley-named-director-does-princeton-plasma-physics-laboratory|archive-date=2018-05-16}}</ref>

As director, Cowley's policy has been to de-emphasize nuclear fusion and high temperature plasma research, turning PPPL into a broad-based laboratory for plasma physics, including low temperature plasmas. This effort involved the construction of a new building at PPPL, the Princeton Plasma Innovation Center (PPIC). PPIC provides laboratory space for plasma-related research areas new to PPPL, including microelectronics, quantum sensors and devices, and sustainability sciences, as well as housing fusion theoretical and computational scientists. He stated he planned for low temperature plasma science to account for 30-50% of the total in future, compared to prior fusion predominance.<ref name="science20"/>

At the same time as de-emphasizing fusion, his main stated priority has been to recover the [[NSTX-U]] [[tokamak]] from its 2016 failure. NSTX-U was the US's flagship fusion experiment, and its failure under Cowley's predecessor "strained the lab's relations with DOE"<ref name="science20">{{cite journal|title=Rekindling the flame|date=7 February 2020|journal=Science|volume=367|issue=6478|doi=10.1126/science.367.6478.618|url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.367.6478.618|last=Cho|first=Adrian|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson DeVoe |first=Jeanne |date=13 May 2024 |title=PPPL looks to the future as it breaks ground on the Princeton Plasma Innovation Center |url=https://www.pppl.gov/news/2024/pppl-looks-future-it-breaks-ground-princeton-plasma-innovation-center |access-date=29 September 2025 |website=Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Harrison |first=Andrew |date=16 May 2024 |title=This is magic |url=https://centraljersey.com/2024/05/16/a-long-time-in-the-making-2/ |access-date=29 September 2025 |work=Central Jersey}}</ref> As of August 2020, NSTX-U was expected to re-start in late 2021.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=US Department of Energy|url=https://www.energy.gov/articles/department-energy-announces-21-million-fusion-energy-instrumentation|date=3 August 2020|title=Department of Energy Announces $21 Million for Fusion Energy Instrumentation}}</ref> As of 2026, NSTX-U was expected to re-start in 2027.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iter.org/node/20687/heart-nstx-u-arrives-princeton|title=The heart of NSTX-U arrives in Princeton|date=22 June 2026|last=Shea|first=Addison|publisher=ITER Organization}}</ref>

Cowley has also expressed a strong commitment to basic science research, including astrophysics. At the unveiling of the Facility for Laboratory Reconnection Experiments (FLARE) in June 2025, Cowley said the experiment – which is designed to study [[magnetic reconnection]] —  represents the next generation of research into fundamental plasma physics and will serve as a collaborative research platform for scientists worldwide.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Fazelpoor |first=Matthew |date=16 June 2025 |title=PPPL launches FLARE for next-gen plasma research |url=https://njbiz.com/pppl-flare-plasma-research-launch/ |access-date=29 September 2025 |work=NJ Biz}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosen |first=Raphael |date=12 June 2025 |title=Unprecedented new device at PPPL will help to unravel the mysteries of the universe |url=https://www.pppl.gov/news/2025/unprecedented-new-device-pppl-will-help-unravel-mysteries-universe |access-date=29 September 2025 |website=Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory}}</ref>

Cowley supports integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into fusion system design. He told an audience at his University of Oxford Lamb Lecture that integrated modeling systems "with multiscale simulations, plus AI surrogates, plus simulations of the neutrons, simulations of the damage, and simulations of the engineering to try to design a better fusion system" are needed to design the ideal fusion system.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bQWoXNOWUhE |title=Lamb Lecture 2025 - 'Fusion energy: why, how and when' by Professor Steve Cowley. |date=2025-06-13 |last=Department of Physics University of Oxford |access-date=2025-09-29 |via=YouTube}}</ref> StellFoundry is one such project at PPPL, using AI to try to find the ideal configuration for stellarators.

Cowley has also argued in favor of larger investment in physical fusion experiments, arguing that "a digital solution is not enough", calling for "investments in the tens of billions of dollars" to build a fusion pilot plant. He also advocated developing a highly skilled workforce and international collaborations. He stated the belief that "clean, safe, sustainable fusion reactors" will provide baseload power generation "by the end of this [21st] century".<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-08-20 |title=Opinion {{!}} The world-saving potential of nuclear fusion just got a huge boost |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2024/08/20/artificial-intelligence-nuclear-fusion-research/ |access-date=2025-09-29 |work=The Washington Post|language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Cowley was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2014|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2014]]. His biography reads:

{{blockquote|Steven Cowley is a leading plasma theorist and currently chief executive officer at the UK Atomic Energy Authority. Much of his research career has been devoted to modelling and understanding plasma turbulence in nuclear fusion, a phenomenon that must be controlled to achieve stable fusion.

Nuclear fusion will offer future generations a cleaner and safer source of energy and has the potential to meet the majority of the world's energy demands. At present, however, more energy is required to feed the process than can be produced. Steven is leading the UK's participation in ITER, an experimental reactor that is set to make nuclear fusion commercially viable.

Steven's interest in plasmas extends to those found on a large scale throughout the Universe. He showed that these astrophysical plasmas also invariably exhibit turbulence, which amplifies and shapes their magnetic fields. Steven presented a 2009 [[TED (conference)|TED talk]] entitled Fusion is Energy's Future and received the 2012 [[Glazebrook Medal]] from the Institute of Physics, which rewards leadership in a physics context.<ref name=royale>{{cite web|author=Anon|year=2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306135347/https://royalsociety.org/people/steven-cowley-11272/ |archive-date=2016-03-06 |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/steven-cowley-11272/ |title=Professor Steven Cowley FREng FRS }} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|"All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." --{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |access-date=2016-03-09 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925220834/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archive-date=2015-09-25 }}}}</ref>}}

His certificate of election reads: {{blockquote|Professor Cowley is currently chief executive officer at the UK Atomic Energy Authority and Professor at Imperial College. Over the last twenty years he has played a leading role in developing the [[Multi-scale approaches|multi-scale approach]] to computing the [[Plasma (physics)|plasma]] [[turbulence]] in [[List of fusion experiments|fusion experiments]]. Now such computations routinely reproduce experimental results. Multi-scale computational tools will be central to the successful development of fusion power. He discovered a key mechanism for the observed explosive eruptions from confined plasmas. Using analysis and computations Cowley and collaborators have shown that [[astrophysical plasma]]s are invariably turbulent. They have described the multi-scale spectra and structure of this turbulence and how it amplifies and shapes the [[magnetic field]] in the [[Plasma cosmology|large scale plasmas of the universe]].<ref name="royal">{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/fellowship/2014/steven-cowley/ |title = Professor Steven Cowley FRS, Chief Executive Officer, UK Atomic Energy Authority |publisher=The Royal Society |archive-date=2014-08-05 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140805045307/https://royalsociety.org/people/fellowship/2014/steven-cowley/ |location=London}}</ref>}}

Cowley was also elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society|American Physical Society (APS)]] in 1998,<ref>{{Cite web|title=List of Fellows of the American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1998&unit_id=DPP&institution=University+of+California%2C+Los+Angeles|access-date=2021-04-23|language=en}}</ref> the [[Institute of Physics]] (FInstP) in 2004<ref>{{Cite web|title=Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory profile|url=https://plasma.princeton.edu/people/steven-c-cowley|access-date=2021-04-23|language=en}}</ref> and the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]] (FREng) in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|title=List of Fellows of the Royal Academy of Engineering|url=https://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/the-fellowship/list-of-fellows?q=cowley|access-date=2021-04-23|language=en}}</ref> He was awarded an honorary fellowship of the Institute of Engineering and Technology in 2015. In 2011, he was appointed to the UK Government's [[Council for Science and Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=UKAEA Steven Cowley to advise UK government|url=http://www.iter.org/newsline/183/789|access-date=2020-10-23|website=ITER|date=July 2011 |language=en}}</ref>

In the [[2018 Birthday Honours]], Cowley was appointed a [[Knight Bachelor]] for services to science and to the development of nuclear fusion.<ref name="LG">{{London Gazette |issue= 62310 |date= 9 June 2018 |page= B2 |supp= y }}</ref> In July 2019, Cowley was awarded the [[honorary degree]] of [[Doctor of Science]] (''honoris causa'') by the [[University of Lancaster]] for his standing as the international authority on fusion energy.<ref>{{cite web |title=Honorary degree for Professor Sir Steven Cowley |url=https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/sci-tech/about-us/news/honorary-degree-for-professor-sir-steven-cowley |publisher=Lancaster University |access-date=18 July 2019 |language=en}}</ref>

== Family ==
Steven Cowley is the grandson of [[John Duncan Cowley]], who was the director of the School of Librarianship of the University of London. He is also the great-great-nephew of [[Arthur Ernest Cowley|Sir Arthur Ernest Cowley]].

Cowley met his future wife, Margaret Koval, during his graduate studies at Princeton University when she arrived as a new graduate student.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Steve Cowley: The knight who leads the Lab has "the most fun job" |url=https://www.pppl.gov/news/2022/steve-cowley-knight-who-leads-lab-has-%E2%80%9C-most-fun-job%E2%80%9D |access-date=2025-09-29 |website=pppl.gov |language=en}}</ref> Koval worked as an Emmy Award-winning television writer, producer, and director for ABC and PBS.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Margaret Koval {{!}} Producer, Director, Writer |url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0468275/ |access-date=2025-09-29 |publisher=IMDb |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Art News Now {{!}} Independent Arts News Reporting |url=https://artsnewsnow.com/ |access-date=2025-09-29 |website=Art News Now |language=en-US}}</ref> She is now a painter.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Koval Painter |first=Margaret |title=Margaret Koval Painter |url=https://margaretkoval.com/ |access-date=2025-09-29 |website=Margaret Koval Painter |language=en-US}}</ref> They married in 1985, shortly before Cowley defended his doctoral thesis. The couple has two sons.<ref name=":1" />
